** ἄγε**, ἄγετε,
_imperative_ of ἄγω, used as _adverb_, **come on!** frequently in {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, who mostly strengthens it, εἰ δ᾽ ἄγε, νῦν δ᾽ ἄγε, ἄγε δή, ἀλλ᾽ ἄγε}}, in _Attic dialect_ frequently ἄγε νύν{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1011, etc.; before 1 and 2}} _person_ _plural_, ἄγε δὴ τραπείομεν{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.441; ἄγε δὴ στέωμεν 11.348; ἄγε τάμνετε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.332; ἀλλ᾽ ἄγε, Πέρσαι, φροντίδα θώμεθα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 140; ἄγε δὴ καὶ χορὸν ἅψωμεν [prev. author] “Eu.” 307}}; rarely before _1st pers.singular_, ἄγε δὴ.. ἀριθμήσω{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.215}}; before _3rd.pers.plural_, ἀλλ᾽ ἄγε, κήρυκες.. λαὸν.. ἀγειρόντων{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.437; in Prose, ἄγε τοίνυν.. σκοπῶμεν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.5.15}}; followed by ὅπως with _future_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 149; _absolutely_, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 590:—also, ἄγετε,.. λύσασθε 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 803}}; ἄγετε with _1st pers.plural_, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.139, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.76, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 665}}; with _1st pers.singular_, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.139: compare ἄγι.}}
